subject: Post-call: Ledgerly performance qualification — context window & streaming hedges
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Ledgerly performance qualification — context window & streaming hedges

Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. I captured the numbers you mentioned and added a few hedges we typically recommend for the UI streaming + summarization flow.

Key SLO/throughput we heard today:
- Latency: p95 initial token target = 250ms (UI perceived latency).
- Streaming sustain: sub-500ms inter-token latency during streaming for real-time UX.
- Throughput/concurrency: steady-state ~100 RPS global, peak concurrency ~40 simultaneous interactive users per region (EU + US), so plan for ~80 concurrent model contexts across regions.
- Typical payloads: average input ~1,200 tokens (user + context), median output ~600 tokens but some long summarizations up to ~2,800 tokens (bulk summary runs).
- Expected QPS distribution: 70% short-chat (<=512 tokens out), 30% long summarization (>=1000 tokens out).

Implication for context window: if you want to support long summarizations without truncation, we should size for at least 4,000 tokens end-to-end (input + output) with a safety margin. Given your long-tail, we recommend testing with an 8k window for the POC so we can measure memory/KV cache impact and latency tail.

Recommended hedges and what we can run in the POC:
1) Prefix caching: cache common system prompts/user histories to reduce repeated decode work for the first tokens.
2) Chunked/streamed generation for long outputs: emit partial answers as they're generated and backfill final tokens to the client when available. This reduces perceived latency for the UI.
3) Model variant fallbacks: route short-chat to a lower-cost low-latency variant and route long summarizations to a high-capacity variant (or queued batch path).
4) KV/prefix trimming policy: keep most recent 2–3 exchanges in the hot cache and offload older context to a cheap cold store with on-demand fetch for long jobs.
5) Batching knobs: target small batches for interactive traffic (batch size <=8) and larger batches for async summarization jobs.
6) Quantization: test 4-bit quantized variant for long summarization to reduce memory footprint if latency impact is acceptable.

POC proposal (2-week):
- Week 1: import ledgerly token samples (you shared) -> reproduce token distributions, run perf matrix (latency vs window size) for 4k, 8k windows.
- Week 2: enable streaming + prefix caching, run concurrency stress tests to 120 RPS to capture tail behavior and hedges.

Deliverables:
- Perf matrix (p50/p95/p99) across window sizes and model variants.
- Canary configuration for your environment (RBAC-friendly, VPC peering if needed).
- Runbook with recommended fallback policies and cost estimate.

Next steps:
- Can you share 1) a sample of 50 representative inputs/expected outputs (attach as .csv) and 2) confirm whether Ledgerly can provide a dev VPC or whether you want Redwood-hosted canary?
- We'll follow up with a proposed canary timeline and a cost delta estimate for 8k vs 4k windows.

Attachments: ledgerly_token_samples.csv (sample tokenized transcripts), ledgerly_slo_requirements.pdf

Thanks — happy to sync if you want the internal perf matrix format.

— Avery

Thanks Avery — this write-up is exactly what we needed. A couple clarifications from our end:

- The 2,800-token long outputs come from our monthly-statement summarization job; those are run asynchronously today but we also plan to offer an on-demand "summarize this statement" from the UI which is why streaming + interactive tail matters.
- We have a dev VPC and can open a peered subnet for your canary; I will loop in infra to share details once we agree on scope.
- For the POC, can you include an estimated cost delta for moving from a 4k context to an 8k context (both per-hour and projected monthly at our expected 120k requests/month)? Procurement will need ballpark numbers.

Action items for us:
- I'll upload 50 sample transcripts to the Drive folder you linked (ETA EOD today).
- Our SRE will confirm VPC peering readiness by Wednesday.

Small ask: can you add a short checklist of what telemetry we need to capture during the POC (token counts, p95 initial token latency, p99 inter-token gap during streaming, GPU mem high-water marks)? That will help us map our observability.

Thanks — Tom

Thanks Tom — quick reply with an internal POC runbook and telemetry checklist. Avery + Jordan will own the canary setup; I'll own the commercial ask and cost delta.

POC runbook (high level):
- Canary type: Redwood-hosted dev canary in Ledgerly dev VPC via peering.
- Models/variants to test: rwd-small-v2 (low-latency), rwd-medium-q4 (balance), rwd-large (quality).
- Window matrix: 4k, 6k, 8k. Start at 4k to establish baseline.
- Concurrency sweep: 10 / 40 / 80 concurrent model contexts.
- Streaming config: chunk size = 32 tokens, initial send after 4 tokens.
- Batching targets: interactive path batch <=8; async summarization batch up to 64.

Telemetry checklist (deliver to Ledgerly Drive):
- token_count.input (per request)
- token_count.output (per request)
- initial_token_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- inter_token_gap_ms during streaming (p50/p95/p99)
- GPU_memory_bytes high-water (sampled per minute)
- avg_batch_size and batching latency
- fallback events (model-variant or queued-path occurrences)

Commercial note: we will provide a cost-delta estimate for 8k vs 4k windows before kick-off. Marissa will share the preliminary numbers in a separate email (cc'd).

Can we schedule a 30-min sync Thursday to agree on the canary start date once you confirm sample uploads?

— Marissa
